<description>
Alternative approach to #36688, citing the relevant parts of its description:

[quoted text omitted]
Fix this by ignoring the exceptionSet. Except on Windows, where we instead disconnect if its used.

We could instead have set `SO_OOBINLINE` on our sockets, so `recv()` returns any urgent data sent to us (and likely leads us to disconnect the peer). RFC 6093 doesn't forbid this, but the current approach seems more clear and direct to me.

The PR makes two additional changes for clarity:
- wrap the `FD_ISSET` check in `#ifdef WIN32` (no behavior change)
- instead of `if (recvSet || errorSet)`, check `errorSet` separately and earlier (emits a different log message)

Test coverage is introduced in `p2p_socket_errors.py`.

Finally a similar fix is applied to HTTP.
</description>

The RFC says:

[quoted text omitted]
This isn't about a misbehaving sender, but rather about application design (both sides).

[quoted text omitted]
I'm not sure what exactly "this" refers to. It's true that the RFC does not forbid applications from setting `SO_OOBINLINE` if they don't "employ urgent indications".

I do think it's good to document that we don't "employ urgent indications". The absence of the setting implies it, but an actual code comment is more clear.

In any case, I'll drop the comment commit.
